inputs.userGoal: Prepare the VNet-integrated Container Apps environment and NAT gateway infrastructure change approved in conversation; do not deploy yet.
subGoals: Preserve existing Azure resources and agent identities; provision a separately named environment additively.
Keep Consumption app compute and the existing public authenticated demo endpoints; restrict PostgreSQL to verified NAT egress.
Prepare and locally validate only; require separate cost- and migration-aware approval before live operations.
insightsApplied: d1-existing-foundation: use westeurope and the existing dedicated resource group.
d1-existing-environment: retain the original default-network environment; create a new environment.
d1-existing-logs: reference the existing workspace and wire the new environment logs to it.
d1-existing-registry: retain existing immutable image digests and ACR grants.
d1-autonomous-identity: retain the existing UAMI and blueprint federation.
d1-interactive-identity: retain the existing UAMI and blueprint federation.
d1-web-identity: retain the existing runtime UAMI and secret grants.
d1-api-identity: retain the existing runtime UAMI and secret grants.
d1-existing-database: retain the database; update its firewall in the separate app deployment step.
d1-existing-vault: retain stored secrets and existing secret-scoped permissions.
inputs.implementation: Bicep under infra/, invoked opt-in by the existing PowerShell foundation script

reasoning.whyChosen: Operational excellence: reuse existing centralized logging.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Shared logs; no change to existing retention or access controls. Existing workspace keys must never be written to evidence or passed on a command line.

reasoning.whyChosen: Security and operational excellence: one stable outbound IPv4 for the database allowlist.
alternativesConsidered: Public IP prefix for a larger egress pool
reasoning.tradeoffs: Additional public IPv4 charge. Public IP zone redundancy does not make Standard NAT zone-redundant.

reasoning.whyChosen: Reliable deterministic SNAT supported by Container Apps workload profiles environments.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Nonzero hourly and data processing charges; Standard NAT is not zone-redundant. StandardV2 is not currently supported by Container Apps. The published ARM naming table omits NAT gateway length/character limits; validate the chosen name with live ARM preflight before provisioning.

reasoning.whyChosen: Dedicated network boundary needed to attach NAT to the environment infrastructure subnet.
alternativesConsidered: An explicitly supplied compatible existing VNet
reasoning.tradeoffs: No peering or routing to existing networks is added; verify address overlap before deployment.

reasoning.whyChosen: Exclusive delegated subnet with NAT and capacity beyond the /27 workload profiles minimum.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Reserves 512 private addresses; subnet sizing must be selected before environment creation.

reasoning.whyChosen: Workload profiles support NAT egress without requiring Dedicated app compute; a separately named environment preserves the existing one.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Public environment ingress intentionally retained for the authenticated web demo; backends remain internal. Existing app environment IDs cannot be changed in place. The published naming table omits managed environment length limits; validate the chosen name with live ARM preflight.

overallReasoning.summary: Add a separately named networked environment using existing logging. Retain registry, identities, PostgreSQL, Key Vault, original environment, and Entra objects. Record verified NAT egress in foundation evidence and consume it in the app deployer.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: NAT and public IPv4 have recurring charges (research indicates a $0.045/hour example base NAT rate, approximately $32.85/730 hours, plus processing, public IP and bandwidth; this is not a westeurope quote). Public authenticated web ingress, existing password-based PostgreSQL/Key Vault storage and existing observability are deliberately retained; a private-data/Entra database redesign, WAF, additional telemetry and multi-zone NAT are out of scope. No live inventory, subscription policy, capacity, final name validation or pricing verification has been performed.

plan.validation: Preparation approved and implemented. Bicep template and parameters compile with exit 0; latest Network API schemas produce BCP081 type-availability warnings even after compiler upgrade. PowerShell syntax, preview guard, preview evidence preservation, mocked confirmed NAT wiring, untagged collisions, app environment guard and egress evidence fallback passed local checks. Checkov is not installed, so its security scan is unverified. No live inventory, policy, ARM validation, what-if, provisioning or cutover checks were run. Deployment remains unauthorized and requires security review plus explicit risk-aware approval. Abort if networking preview modifies or deletes referenced resources.
implementationSteps: Generate infra/main.bicep with new network resources and environment; reference existing Log Analytics using listKeys internally, without emitting keys.

Add opt-in EnableStableEgress to Provision-D1Foundation.ps1 with a new environment name; run ARM validate and what-if before incremental deployment, check ownership and do not reconfigure unrelated resources.

Write environment name/domain, subnet ID, NAT/public IP resource IDs and ContainerAppsEgressIps into foundation evidence. Deploy-D1ContainerApps.ps1 consumes this evidence when no explicit egress override is supplied.
Rerun Entra provisioning with all three existing child ID pairs after foundation deployment to add the new web redirect URI; preserve the old redirect until cutover verification.
If apps already exist in the original environment, stop before database/firewall changes and require an explicit app migration strategy; never update an app in the wrong environment.
Deploy apps to the new environment using existing image digests and identities; update PostgreSQL firewall only with verified NAT IPs, then run health, sign-in, OBO and autonomous flow checks.
Keep the original environment until successful cutover. Cleanup is separately authorized and is never automatic.
